glosses.notes: Personal thoughts or feelings that come after reading, seeing, hearing, or going through something.

examples.sentence: 参观完父亲年轻时工作的老工厂以后，弟弟一路都没怎么说话，回家坐下才慢慢把自己的感想一条一条写在本子上。
老师没有急着让大家交报告，而是先让每个人围着桌子谈谈看完那部片子后的感想，看看谁真的注意到了那些小细节。
她把这次旅行拍的照片送给奶奶时，还顺手夹了一页感想，说这一路最难忘的不是风景，而是路上认识的人。

example_translations.translation: After visiting the old factory where Father had worked when he was young, my younger brother hardly said anything on the way home. Only after sitting down did he slowly write his impressions out in his notebook one by one.

The teacher did not rush everyone into handing in a report. Instead, she first had each person sit around the table and talk about their reflections after watching the film, to see who had really noticed the small details.

When she gave Grandma the photos from this trip, she also tucked in a page of thoughts, saying that what she would remember most from the journey was not the scenery but the people she got to know on the way.

glosses.notes: Usually means a fountain pen rather than a general pen, often with attention to handwriting, ink, and how it feels in the hand.

examples.sentence: 爷爷现在写信还是只用那支旧钢笔，说换成别的笔以后手上没有分量，字也写不出从前那样了。
她写名字前先把带来的钢笔在纸上试了两下，怕路上出了问题，等真要用时反而不能写字。
老师用钢笔改作业的时候，最后一排的学生一直在抄答案，他只好停下来再把前面的过程讲一遍。

example_translations.translation: Grandpa still uses only that old fountain pen when he writes letters. He says that once he switches to another kind of pen, it no longer feels substantial in his hand, and his writing no longer comes out the way it used to.
Before writing her name, she tested the fountain pen she had brought on the paper twice, afraid something had gone wrong on the way and that when she really needed it, it would not write.
While the teacher was correcting homework with a fountain pen, the students in the last row kept copying the answers, so he had to stop and explain the earlier steps once more.

glosses.notes: The source seed keeps the OCR form 港又. It corresponds to 港口 'port'; examples preserve the seed spelling so the live validator can match the shared source lexicon.

examples.sentence: 台风消息一出来，海边那个港又就忙了起来，很多还没回来的船都得赶在天黑前先慢慢靠进去。
这个老港又白天一直有人搬东西，到了晚上却只剩远处的灯和海边的风，所以第一次来的人总会多看一会儿。
城里后来把旧港又边上的房子修好了，所以那一带慢慢又有了人。

example_translations.translation: As soon as the typhoon warning came out, that port by the sea grew busy. Many ships that had not yet returned had to slowly come in before dark.

This old harbor has people moving goods around all day, but by night only the distant lights and the sea wind remain, so people visiting for the first time always end up standing there a little longer.
Later, the city repaired the houses beside the old port, and little by little people returned to that area.

glosses.notes: A work post or assigned position, especially in an office, school, factory, hospital, or shift schedule.

examples.sentence: 医院这次重新排岗位的时候，护士长先问了每个人家里的情况，尽量把夜班留给住得近又方便照顾病人的人。
他原来只想找一份离家近的工作，后来才知道这个岗位每天都要见很多人。
老师让学生去不同岗位体验半天以后再回来写记录，这样大家才知道食堂、门口和值班室其实都不轻松。

example_translations.translation: When the hospital rearranged its posts this time, the head nurse first asked about everyone's family situation and tried to leave the night shifts to those who lived nearby and could more easily take care of patients.
He had originally wanted only a job close to home, but later learned that this position required meeting many people every day.

After having the students spend half a day experiencing different posts and then come back to write a record, the teacher hoped they would understand that the cafeteria, the entrance, and the duty room were all real work.

glosses.notes: Can describe senior management or the upper floors and upper-level residents of a building, depending on the context.

examples.sentence: 公司高层开会讨论新厂安排时，谈得最久的不是机器，而是新来员工住哪里、孩子上学远不远这些很实际的问题。
这栋楼的高层住户前几天一直说水太小，物业后来一层一层查上去，才发现是通到楼顶的那根老水管出了问题。
消息传出来以后，店里的普通员工还没弄清楚细节，反而是总部高层先赶到现场，把后面可能影响顾客的地方一项一项问清楚。

example_translations.translation: When senior management met to discuss arrangements for the new factory, what they spent the longest time on was not the machines, but practical issues such as where the new workers would live and how far their children would have to travel to school.

Residents on the upper floors of this building had been saying for days that the water flow was too weak. Only after the property staff checked floor by floor did they realize the old pipe leading up to the roof was the problem.

After the news spread, the ordinary employees in the shop still did not understand the details, but senior people from headquarters had already reached the scene and started asking about every point that might affect customers later.

glosses.notes: Describes skill or technique as extremely strong, polished, and hard to match.

examples.sentence: 护士的手法很高超，针一下就打完了，孩子后来只看着前面的画。
那位修钟表的老师傅本事实在高超，外公本来都准备把表收起来了，结果他坐了一晚上又让指针慢慢走了。
大家看了以后才知道他的技术很高超。

example_translations.translation: The nurse's technique was superb. The shot was over in an instant, and afterward the child only stared at the picture in front.
That old watch repairman was truly masterful. Grandpa had already been ready to put the watch away for good, but after one evening of work, the man got the hands moving again.
Only after seeing it did everyone realize how superb his technique was.

glosses.notes: Usually appears in compounds such as 高等教育, 高等学校, or 高等数学 to mean higher-level or advanced.

examples.sentence: 家里原来没人读过高等学校，所以姐姐拿到录取通知那天，奶奶把信封拿在手里看了很久，连晚饭都忘了先拿出来。
老师讲到高等教育的费用时，没有只说学费，还提醒大家早点了解住宿、路费和书本这些后面一直会用到的钱。
他原来最怕高等数学，后来跟着老师学了几次，也敢自己做题了。

example_translations.translation: No one in the family had ever attended higher education before, so on the day my older sister received her admission notice, Grandma held the envelope in her hands and looked at it for a long time, even forgetting to bring dinner out first.

When the teacher spoke about the cost of higher education, she did not mention only tuition. She also reminded everyone to learn early about the money they would keep needing later for housing, travel, and books.
He used to fear higher mathematics the most, but after studying with the teacher a few times, he gradually dared to do the problems by himself.

glosses.notes: Describes products, services, or market segments positioned at the high end in price, image, or expected quality.

examples.sentence: 父亲说这家店的高端产品看着都很漂亮，就是价钱太高。
公司想打入高端市场，所以样品刚做好，高层就把颜色、材料和顾客第一次打开盒子时的感觉来回改了好几次。
她本来以为高端酒店的服务只是房间更大，住进去以后才发现，真正让人安心的是很多小细节都有人提前想到。

example_translations.translation: Father said the high-end products in this shop all looked beautiful; the only problem was that the prices were too high.

The company wanted to break into the premium market, so as soon as the sample was ready, senior staff revised the colors, the materials, and the feeling customers would get when opening the box for the first time again and again.

She had assumed that service in a high-end hotel simply meant larger rooms, but after staying there she realized that what truly put people at ease was the way so many small details had been thought through in advance.

glosses.notes: The busiest or highest point in traffic, demand, tourism, flow, or another rising pattern.

examples.sentence: 早高峰刚到，地铁口那家卖早点的小店就排到门外去了，老板连找钱都得一边说话一边飞快地算。
每到假期高峰，山上那条最窄的路不到九点就开始慢慢堵住，所以很多带孩子的家长天一亮就先出发了。
医院把早上的挂号时间往前调了半小时以后，原来最挤的那段高峰总算散开一些，老人不用天没亮就先来门口等了。

example_translations.translation: As soon as the morning rush hour started, the breakfast shop by the subway exit had a line stretching outside, and the owner had to calculate change at top speed while still talking to customers.
During the holiday peak, the narrowest road up the mountain starts to clog before nine o'clock, so many parents traveling with children set out as soon as it gets light.
After the hospital moved the morning registration time half an hour earlier, the busiest peak period finally spread out a little, and older people no longer had to wait at the entrance before dawn.

glosses.notes: Describes someone's character, values, or behavior as morally admirable rather than selfish or petty.

examples.sentence: 捡到钱包以后，他没有先看里面有多少钱，而是站在原地等那个找钱包的人回来，旁边的人都说这种做法看着简单，其实很高尚。
奶奶常说，答应过别人的事要认真去做，这样才谈得上高尚。
老师给孩子讲那位老医生的故事时，没有故意把话说得多感人，只是让大家自己想想，为什么那么多人一直记得他那种高尚的心。

example_translations.translation: After finding the wallet, he did not first look to see how much money was inside. He simply stood where he was and waited for the person looking for the wallet to come back, and the people nearby said that while the act looked simple, it was actually very noble.
Grandma often says that if you have promised something to someone else, you need to do it seriously; only then does it count as noble.

When the teacher told the children the story of that old doctor, he did not try to make it sound overly moving. He only asked everyone to think for themselves about why so many people still remembered that doctor's noble heart.

glosses.notes: An expert with notably strong practical skill, often in games, crafts, repair, cooking, or another hands-on field.

examples.sentence: 周末一到，来找他的人都知道他是高手。
店里那台老机器谁都修不好，最后还是请来以前在厂里干过很多年的高手，一边听声音一边就找到了问题。
后来大家才知道他是高手。

example_translations.translation: As soon as the weekend comes, the people who come looking for him all know that he is an expert.
No one in the shop could repair that old machine, and in the end they had to invite an expert who had worked in the factory for many years. He found the problem just by listening to the sound.
Only later did everyone realize that he was an expert.

glosses.notes: A fixed noun meaning high and new technology, commonly used for high-tech industry, equipment, zones, and exhibitions.

examples.sentence: 这座城市这几年多了不少做高新技术的地方，所以边上的小店也越来越多。
医生说这套高新技术设备能帮很多病人。
老师让学生自己看高新技术怎么帮人做事。

example_translations.translation: In recent years, this city has added many places doing high-tech work, so there are more and more small shops nearby as well.
The doctor said that this piece of high-tech equipment could help many patients.
The teacher let the students see for themselves how high technology helps people do things.

glosses.notes: A plateau or highland region, often discussed with altitude, weather, travel, or breathing.

examples.sentence: 第一次上高原的人一下车往往不敢走太快，因为只是把包提到门口，胸口都可能先觉得有点发紧。
医生提醒准备去高原的人，前两天别走太快，不舒服要马上说。
火车开进高原以后，孩子一直看着窗外。

example_translations.translation: People going up to a plateau for the first time often do not dare walk too fast right after getting out of the car, because even carrying a bag to the doorway can already make their chest feel tight.
The doctor reminded people preparing to go to the plateau not to walk too fast during the first two days and to speak up immediately if they felt unwell.
After the train entered the plateau, the child kept looking out the window.

glosses.notes: A submitted article, manuscript, or written piece sent to an editor, publisher, or news desk.

examples.sentence: 编辑把那份稿件退回来时没有直接说不行，而是在旁边写了很多问题，连哪里该删、哪里该补都写得很清楚。
报社那天一下收到太多稿件，值班的人只好先按时间排好，再把内容差不多的放在一起，免得后面重复看很多次。
她出门前又检查了一遍邮件，确认稿件和照片都传过去了，才敢把手机放回包里，安心去车站等车。

example_translations.translation: When the editor sent that manuscript back, he did not simply say it would not do. Instead, he wrote down many questions beside it, and even the places that should be cut and added were explained very clearly.

The newspaper office received far too many submissions that day, so the person on duty had to sort them by time first and then place similar pieces together, to avoid reading the same kind of thing over and over later.

Before leaving, she checked her email once again to make sure both the manuscript and the photos had been sent through, and only then did she dare put her phone back into her bag and head to the station in peace.

glosses.notes: A draft text or script that is still being revised, often for a speech, article, report, or performance.

examples.sentence: 弟弟把稿子背了很多次，上台以后第一句还是说慢了。
记者把采访录音听完以后，先写了个很粗的稿子，吃完晚饭再回来把细节一段一段补齐，这样第二天改起来会轻松很多。
奶奶看完我写给学校的稿子以后，只改了几个词，却一下让整段话听起来更真诚，也更像我平时会说的话。

example_translations.translation: My younger brother went over the draft many times, but after getting on stage, he still said the first sentence too slowly.

After listening through the interview recording, the reporter first wrote a rough draft and then came back after dinner to fill in the details section by section, which would make revising it the next day much easier.
After reading the script I had written for school, Grandma changed only a few words, but somehow the whole piece suddenly sounded more sincere and more like something I would really say.

glosses.notes: To cut something apart with a blade or edge, and by extension to split things apart or divide them sharply.

examples.sentence: 医生检查以后说，伤口虽然是被玻璃割的，可是不深，只要这几天别碰水，慢慢就会长好。
父亲天一亮就去院子里割草，因为天气预报说下午可能有雨，他怕到时候地一湿，后面连机器都推不动。
他们谈分工的时候最怕的不是活太多，而是有人想先把责任和好处割开，最后谁也不肯让一点。

example_translations.translation: After examining it, the doctor said that although the wound had been cut by glass, it was not deep. As long as it did not touch water for the next few days, it would slowly heal.

Father went out to cut the grass as soon as it got light, because the weather forecast said it might rain in the afternoon and he was afraid that once the ground got wet, even the machine would be hard to push.

When they discussed how to divide the work, what worried them most was not that there was too much to do, but that someone might first separate responsibility from the benefits, leaving no one willing to give even a little.

glosses.notes: A somewhat formal verb for singing, often used in organized, staged, or collective contexts.

examples.sentence: 社区活动中心每周三晚上都有人在楼下歌唱，楼上的人听久了，连哪一段快一点、哪一段慢一点都差不多记住了。
老师不是一开始就要求孩子站上台歌唱，而是先让他们围着钢琴把声音放开，慢慢习惯大家一起唱出来的感觉。
这些学生一到歌唱课，就会一起歌唱，平时最安静的几个也一样。

example_translations.translation: Every Wednesday evening, people sing downstairs at the community center, and the people upstairs hear it so often that they have almost memorized which part is a little faster and which part is a little slower.

The teacher did not ask the children to stand on stage and sing right from the start. Instead, she first had them gather around the piano, open up their voices, and slowly get used to what it felt like to sing together.
As soon as these students get to singing class, they sing together, including the ones who are usually the quietest.

glosses.notes: Means next door or the place and people right beside one's home, room, or shop.

examples.sentence: 隔壁那家店刚换了老板以后，母亲去了几次，后来一看见他就知道她常买什么。
隔壁的人听见声音以后先来敲门。
我们后来先认识了隔壁的人。

example_translations.translation: After the shop next door changed owners, Mother went a few times, and later on he would recognize her as soon as he saw her and know what she usually bought.
After hearing the noise, the person next door came first to knock.
Later on, the first people we got to know were the neighbors next door.

glosses.notes: Usually refers to revolution or revolutionary things in historical, political, or social contexts.

examples.sentence: 老师讲革命时候的事时，没有只让大家背时间，而是拿出几封老信，让学生自己想那些人为什么愿意那样做。
外公在里面听革命歌曲听了半天，出来以后还跟我讲了几句。
奶奶拿着那张革命年代的老照片，看了很久。

example_translations.translation: When the teacher talked about life during the revolutionary period, he did not just make everyone memorize dates. He took out several old letters and asked the students to think about why those people had been willing to act that way.
Grandpa listened to revolutionary songs inside for a long time, and after he came out he even repeated a few lines to me.
Grandma held that old photo from the revolutionary era and looked at it for a long time.

glosses.notes: An individual unit or person considered on its own rather than only as part of a larger group.

examples.sentence: 医生解释方案时一直强调，每个病人的身体情况都不一样，所以真正怎么治，还得看这个个体当时的反应。
个体情况不一样，所以老师不能都用一个办法。
研究的人后来发现，个体每天做什么也很重要。

example_translations.translation: When explaining the treatment plan, the doctor kept emphasizing that every patient's physical condition was different, so the real decision about how to treat them still depended on how that individual reacted at the time.
Each individual is different, so the teacher cannot use exactly the same method for everyone.
Researchers later found that what an individual does each day also matters a great deal.

glosses.notes: A formal verb meaning to give, grant, or provide something such as help, trust, rights, time, or support.

examples.sentence: 老师没有直接替他做决定，只是在他最乱的时候先给予一点时间和信任，让他自己把真正想做的事慢慢说出来。
医院给老人办完手续以后，还给予家属一张写着注意事项的纸，怕大家一忙起来把回家后的细节忘了。
那位老板知道孩子家里难，所以除了给工作，还主动给予住的地方和头一个月最基本的生活照顾。

example_translations.translation: The teacher did not make the decision for him directly. She first gave him some time and trust when he felt most confused, letting him slowly say what he truly wanted to do.

After the hospital finished the paperwork for the elderly man, it also provided the family with a sheet of instructions, afraid that if everyone got too busy, they would forget the details to watch for after going home.
That boss knew the child's family was having a hard time, so besides giving him a job, he also took the initiative to provide a place to stay and basic living support for the first month.

glosses.notes: Used after a person or place to mean right in front of it, by it, or at someone's side.

examples.sentence: 孩子一看见久没回家的父亲，就抱着书包跑到他跟前，连鞋都来不及先换，好像怕人下一秒又要走。
奶奶把常用的药都放在床跟前，因为夜里要是一下找不到，手一摸到就知道先吃哪个。
讨论最热闹的时候，经理把那份刚改完的表摆到大家跟前，让每个人先低头看两分钟，再决定后面还要不要继续争。

example_translations.translation: The moment the child saw his father, who had not been home for a long time, he ran right up to him with his schoolbag still on, not even taking time to change his shoes, as if he feared the man might leave again the next second.
Grandma keeps her usual medicine by the bed, because if she cannot find it right away during the night, she can tell which one to take first as soon as she touches it.

At the liveliest point in the discussion, the manager placed the newly revised chart in front of everyone and had each person look down at it for two minutes before deciding whether the argument needed to continue.

glosses.notes: To follow behind, accompany, or go along with someone, something, or a lead.

examples.sentence: 导游说完注意事项以后，让大家别只顾着拍照，一定跟随前面那个人走，不然过两个路口就很容易走散。
小狗刚到家那几天一直跟随母亲，母亲去哪儿，它就去哪儿。
这位年轻记者刚开始工作时常跟随老同事出门，不只是学着问问题，也学着看见别人没注意到的小细节。

example_translations.translation: After explaining the safety instructions, the guide told everyone not to focus only on taking photos and to make sure they followed the person in front, or else it would be easy to get separated after passing two intersections.
During the first few days after arriving home, the puppy kept following Mother; wherever she went, it went too.

When this young reporter first started work, he often followed older coworkers out on assignments. He was learning not only how to ask questions, but also how to notice small details other people missed.

glosses.notes: Can mean tracking someone or something physically, or following up on a condition, case, or development over time.

examples.sentence: 快递迟迟没到，父亲晚上又打开手机跟踪那条送货路线，结果才发现车下午进错了另一个小区。
医生让她回家以后继续跟踪体温和睡眠，只要哪一项再有明显变化，就把时间和情况马上记下来。
学校没有把那次意外处理完就算了，而是安排老师继续跟踪几个孩子后面的状态，看看谁还需要单独谈一谈。

example_translations.translation: The package still had not arrived, so Father opened his phone again that evening to track the delivery route, and only then discovered that the vehicle had entered the wrong residential complex that afternoon.
The doctor told her to keep monitoring her temperature and sleep after going home, and to write down the time and circumstances immediately if either one changed noticeably again.

The school did not simply consider the matter finished after handling that incident. It arranged for teachers to continue following up on the condition of several children afterward to see who still needed a separate talk.

glosses.notes: This bound form often appears in words like 公家 or 公事 to mean public or official, and it can also describe fairness or impartiality when used on its own.

examples.sentence: 这笔钱是公家的，每次有人买东西回来都要把花了多少写清楚，谁也不能觉得差一点没关系。
村里那位老人最让人服气，就是他说话一直很公，不管跟谁更熟，先听完两边的话再慢慢让大家坐下商量。
父亲常说办公事要公一点，不能因为认识对方就少查一道手续，不然最后吃亏的还是后面排队的人。

example_translations.translation: This money belongs to the public side, so whenever someone comes back from buying something, they have to clearly write down how much was spent; no one can treat a small difference as unimportant.

What makes that old man in the village so respected is that he is always fair in the way he speaks. No matter whom he is closer to, he first listens to both sides and then slowly has everyone sit down and talk it through.

Father often says that when handling official business, one should be a little more impartial. You cannot skip a step just because you know the other person, or else the ones who suffer in the end will be the people lining up behind them.
